name: Ka'b ibn Zuhayr
bio: A poet of the first rank from Najd, already famous before Islam, and of a family steeped in poetry: his father was Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma, author of one of the Mu'allaqat, and his brother Bujayr, his son Uqba and his grandson al-Awwam were all poets. When Islam came he satirised the Prophet, who declared his life forfeit. He then came to Medina asking for safety, having become a Muslim, and recited «Banat Su'ad»; the Prophet pardoned him, and by one report gave him his own mantle. The poem has drawn many commentaries, expansions and imitations, and was translated into Italian and French. He died in 26 AH (645 CE).
